title: City Reliquary

card.teaser: An identity for a museum of everyday objects, built on a negative-space CR mark.

summary: A visual identity for City Reliquary, a community-focused New York City museum, built around a collage-like CR mark formed from overlapping rectangular frames.
meta: CR mark, identity system, posters, signage

hero.alt: A red t-shirt printed with the white City Reliquary mark, worn against a graffitied wall.

text: City Reliquary celebrates New York City's history through everyday objects, personal collections, and overlooked artifacts. The identity draws on the idea of collecting and preserving fragments of history, using a collage of frames to create a distinctive mark that reflects the museum's approach.

rows.heading: Objects worth keeping
rows.body: City Reliquary collects everyday artifacts and the stories attached to them, so I started with the museum itself: the red storefront, the script sign, the cabinet-of-curiosities feel. Then I looked at how Cooper Hewitt, the American Folk Art Museum and the Museum of the City of New York hold a name inside a simple shape.
rows.caption: Museum notes and logo references.
rows.alt: Research and references for the City Reliquary identity.

rows.heading: Finding the mark
rows.body: I started with nine small thumbnails, trying the C and R as blocks, circles, a stacked name and a half circle. Then I developed three: a tower, a skyline and a cluster of heavy boxes. The cluster won, because the negative space between the boxes could do the work of the second letter.
rows.caption: Mark sketches.
rows.alt: Sketches of the City Reliquary CR mark.

finalDesign: The tower and skyline sketches were the obvious New York answers, and the museum isn't about landmarks. It's about small things people didn't want to lose. I also dropped the stacked CITY / RELIQUARY lockup, because the Museum of the City of New York already does that. The cluster of boxes stayed, in the red of the museum's own storefront. The C and R come from the gaps between the boxes, the way a shelf of objects makes a shape.
pull: The museum isn't about landmarks. It's about small things people didn't want to lose.
